pages.text: A catalyst holds a molecule on its surface just long enough to change it. Too weakly and nothing sticks, too tightly and nothing leaves: plotted against the binding energy, the activity is a $(thing)volcano$() (Sabatier). The coverage of a surface follows $(thing)θ = KP/(1 + KP)$() (Langmuir).

The $(item)Catalyst Formulator$() makes the catalysts more cheaply than the Chemical Reactor: set the metal loading and the calcination temperature so the binding sits at the volcano's peak - but calcine too hot and the metal sinters. It also makes the $(item)Nickel Catalyst$(), for hydrogenation.
The $(item)Regeneration Kiln$() now has a console too: burn the coke off hot enough and with air enough, but below about 900 K, where the metal starts to sinter. 90% must come back.
